articles.title: Seth Rogen Says Brad Pitt and ‘12 Years a Slave’ Cast Would Visit ‘This Is the End’ Set to ‘Perk Up’ Because They Were ‘in a Bummed-Out Headspace’ While Filming
articles.summary: Seth Rogen and Brad Pitt spent time together while shooting very different films in 2013. Rogen recalled Pitt, Michael Fassbender, Chiwetel Ejiofor and other cast members from “12 Years a Slave” spending time on the set of his comedy “This Is the End” while the two films were both shooting in New…
body: “Actually, what’s so weird is I had met him — we made ‘This Is the End’ at the same time they made ’12 Years a Slave’ in New Orleans together,” Rogen told podcast host Josh Horowitz. “Understandably, the cast and crew of ’12 Years a Slave’ were in a bummed-out headspace a lot of the time.”

“12 Years a Slave” starred Ejiofor as a free Black man named Solomon Northup who was kidnapped in 1841 and sold into slavery in Louisiana. Fassbender played plantation owner Edwin Epps and Pitt played an abolitionist named Samuel Bass who helped Northup regain his freedom.

Meanwhile, Rogen was shooting “This Is the End” with Jay Baruchel, James Franco, Jonah Hill, Craig Robinson, Danny McBride and a host of other celebrities. The actors played dramatized versions of themselves in a bizarre apocalyptic scene at a Hollywood house party.

articles.title: Jeff Goldblum Performs a Piano Medley and Reflects on His Career at Marrakech Film Festival: ‘The Stories That We Tell Matter’
articles.summary: Jeff Goldblum was honored with a tribute award at the Marrakech Film Festival on Saturday, delighting the audience with a surprise piano performance before reflecting on more than half a century in cinema, giving a heartfelt speech in which he thanked his many on-screen collaborators and insisted…
body: After a tribute video showcased iconic Goldblum performances across his career, including roles in “Invasion of the Body Snatchers,” “The Fly,” “Jurassic Park” and “Independence Day,” the curtain rose to reveal the actor — an accomplished pianist and jazz musician — seated behind a grand piano, from which he performed a medley of songs before a rapt crowd.

Accepting the award after a lengthy standing ovation, Goldblum thanked the many screenwriters, directors and actors who showed faith in him through the years and insisted that moviemaking remains as vital an art form as ever.

“I believe that the stories that we tell matter,” the actor said. “At their best, films let us sit in the dark beside strangers and see the world through somebody else’s eyes. They remind us that we lucky creatures have an unfathomable measure of commonality, and they put to shame all those petty things which seem to divide us.

“Movies also help us imagine something better — a world that works for everyone,” he continued. “That’s a planet toward which I want to keep working for as long as I have breath in my body, and with every story that I might still have the privilege to tell.”

articles.title: Russell Crowe’s Request to Shoot ‘A Beautiful Mind’ Chronologically Added $1 Million to the Budget, Says Ron Howard: ‘It Was the Right Kind of Investment’
articles.summary: “A Beautiful Mind” director Ron Howard recently called Russell Crowe’s suggestion to shoot the film in order, which cost the studio an additional $1 million, was “the right kind of investment.” The 2001 film follows mathematician John Forbes Nash Jr.
body: “A Beautiful Mind” director Ron Howard recently called Russell Crowe ’s suggestion to shoot the film in order, which cost the studio an additional $1 million, was “the right kind of investment.”
“I am convinced it was the right kind of investment,” Howard told People magazine. “Russell certainly carried his part of the bargain with a brave and consistently detailed performance.”

The director likened the approach to George Lucas’ on “American Graffiti,” where the “Star Wars” helmsman shot in sequence to highlight the “wear and tear” of night shoots on screen. Filming “A Beautiful Mind” in order could help Crowe develop a natural progression in his role.

“Russell had, in passing, requested that we shoot the movie in sequence because the psychiatric journey and the way it would be revealed in the movie would be difficult to calibrate shooting the third act first and the first act second, which is typical for most movies,” Howard said.

articles.title: How the ‘Elsinore’ Makeup Team Transformed Stars Andrew Scott and Olivia Colman to Bring the Story of Ian Charleson to Life
articles.summary: In “Elsinore,” Andrew Scott plays real-life actor Ian Charleson, who performed his final role while dying of AIDS. Written by Stephen Beresford, “Elsinore” follows the deeply emotional and inspirational true story of Charleson as he confronts his mortality with courage, honesty and wit. On Nov.
body: The biopic (currently in theaters) reunites Scott with Olivia Colman, who previously starred alongside him in “Fleabag.” This time, their bond is a special one as Colman plays Margaret Johnson, the doctor who treats Charleson.

For “Elsinore,” both actors needed to transform themselves — not only into the real people they were portraying, but also back to the 1980s. That’s where makeup department head Nadia Stacey played a key role. Stacey, who was honored at last month’s Middleburg Film Festival, spoke about her work and approach to the film, explaining that “when there are real people, you have to be sympathetic to them.”

Stacey described the ’80s as a tricky period to recreate, given it can easily become clichéd. “You immediately imagine everybody had a perm,” she said. “My approach every time is that you shouldn’t notice hair and makeup unless you actually want to notice hair and makeup. The story told itself. I just needed to tell his journey and put us in the era we were in without overdoing it.”

articles.title: ‘I’m opening the cage of a monster’: Taxi Driver scriptwriter Paul Schrader on unleashing AI at 80
articles.summary: Director and Scorsese collaborator is using AI in films and sees its takeover as inevitable, not just in cinema. Paul Schrader was sipping white wine in a Greenwich Village trattoria when he said how he felt about using AI to make films: “I am opening the cage of a monster and I don’t have a…
body: The 80-year-old film-maker behind Taxi Driver, Raging Bull and American Gigolo, is embracing the technology as he enters the final act of a prolific career in which he has collaborated with Martin Scorsese, Robert De Niro, Sigourney Weaver and Richard Gere.

Defying orthodox resistance among the Hollywood guilds to using AI to create synthetic actors, special effects and even scripts, Schrader is doing all of those things. It is part of what he sees as AI’s inevitable takeover, not just of cinema, the art he has pursued for half a century, writing and directing dozens of films to international acclaim, but of humankind more broadly.

“I don’t see, quite frankly, a place for Homo sapiens in the larger scheme of things,” he told the Guardian. “I don’t think there’s a story where we come out on top. In order to create a story where … man defeats the threat of AI – it’s just a bogus story.”

Yet, while directors ranging from his 1970s collaborator Steven Spielberg to the Odyssey’s Christopher Nolan, express deep scepticism about AI, Schrader is running towards, not away from, what he describes as a monster that he fears may soon imprison him.

articles.title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85
articles.summary: The 85-year-old he died in the early hours of Saturday at home in Cornwall, following a recent illness.
body: Peter Fluck, co-creator of award-winning satirical puppet show Spitting Image, has died aged 85.

Spitting Image was immensely popular and sometimes controversial, running from 1984-1996 across 18 seasons, and featured puppet caricatures of celebrities, politicians and royals, including former Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher and Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother.
"The spirit that Spitting Image brought to the country was epoch defining," a family statement said.
"With Roger Law ('Luck and Flaw'), he brought a unique cutting edge to caricaturing that later evolved into a production company that created the TV series Spitting Image," it added.

articles.title: ‘Shakespearean tale of ego, greed and ambition’: the scandalous story of televangelism
articles.summary: Netflix documentary Primetime Preacher$ travels back to a time when evangelism found a dominant place on US television – and the shocking tabloid stories that followed.
body: For three decades, film-maker Joe Berlinger has gripped true-crime buffs with his deep dives into small-town murders and infamous serial killers. His Netflix explorations of John Wayne Gacy and Jeffrey Dahmer helped flip documentary storytelling from viewer homework to a welcome distraction.

After dedicating so much time to the life of Jeffrey Epstein, the kidnapping of JonBenét Ramsey and other unsolved mysteries, Berlinger thought Primetime Preacher$, his new Netflix documentary on America’s televangelist boom, would offer a break. But it turns out that’s a pretty juicy crime story too, about the religious right’s bank job on American politics. “The deeper resonance for me came when I realized that the global televangelism rise actually mirrors the rise of the religious right,” he says. “Religion and politics, from Reagan on, has really changed politics for the worse in my opinion. This was the birth of that.”

articles.title: You Can See Everything’s vibes-check approach is an insult to objective truth
articles.summary: For three hours, Nathan Fielder opts not to quiz convicted criminal Elizabeth Holmes on the details of her deception. Instead, he looks into her eyes and asks if she’s for real. Is that why his film has been so successful? • This article does not contain major spoilers.
body: Sometimes, people who have lied lie about whether or not they’ve lied. They even, on occasion, fail to tell the truth despite having sworn to do so – in court, for instance, or staring deeply into the eyes of someone who is sitting right there.

Is that a shock? Probably not. We all engage in versions of such behaviour every day. We understand that the current climate of mutually clueless echo chambers helps claptrap gain traction. But we can still recognise the difference between little white lies and big red flags. We know that the moment anyone starts using the phrase “my truth” it’s time to cancel the wedding.

You Can See Everything acts as if this isn’t the case. It operates in a realm of smart and artful naivety. In order to interrogate whether or not Elizabeth Holmes, founder of magical medical tech company Theranos, is – as she claims – the tragic victim of a miscarriage of justice, Nathan Fielder moves into the annexe of her home for a few weeks before she starts her 11-year prison term for fraud.
points: For three hours, Nathan Fielder opts not to quiz convicted criminal Elizabeth Holmes on the details of her deception.
Instead, he looks into her eyes and asks if she’s for real.

articles.title: Why Magno Stift From The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping Looks So Familiar
articles.summary: Capitol stylist Magno Stift is bad at his job in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping. The actor who plays him, on the other hand, is highly accomplished.
body: The "Hunger Games" universe is full of wild, larger-than-life characters, especially when we're talking about denizens of the ultra-wealthy and super-powerful Capitol that controls Panem. Every year, during the annual Hunger Games that cull (or "reap") children from each of Panem's tightly controlled and impoverished 12 districts, Capitol citizens help beautify those kids before sending most of them to their deaths, and many Capitol higher-ups pursue plastic surgery and extreme fashion for high-concept looks.

When Magno finally shows up, we see him through Haymitch's eyes: "Magno Stift's sun-leathered skin has been tattooed with a snakeskin pattern. He wears a long shirt made of metal diamonds and no visible pants. His sandals lace all the way up to his pelvis, and from each of his ears dangle tiny, living garter snakes that twist and turn in misery." Eventually, he stops showing up to work when one of his wearable reptiles poisons him. So, why does Magno look familiar in the movie?

articles.title: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Feasting With $120M+ in Franchise’s Box Office Comeback
articles.summary: Lionsgate's latest title notched the fourth-best opening Friday in the six-movie dystopian series, representing a major revival after 2023's 'The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes.'
body: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping has begun to ignite the box office.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping will notch the fifth-biggest opening in Lionsgate history, as it also stands at No. 5 among 2026 domestic openings for all studios. It represents the highest-grossing launch for the careers of stars Glenn Close, Jesse Plemons, Kieran Culkin and Elle Fanning. This weekend’s haul also brings the Hunger Games franchise’s box office total to roughly $3.437 billion to make it the studio’s highest-grossing franchise ever, besting The Twilight Saga.

Lionsgate had projected The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping to gross north of $80 million, but other sources expected that it would collect between $100 million and $130 million, which now looks to be the case. Adapting author Suzanne Collins’ prequel novel that was published last year, director Francis Lawrence ‘s movie carries a production budget of roughly $150 million as it revitalizes the franchise in telling a story set 24 years before the events of Collins’ original 2008 book.
